title: fix(plugins): keep a working plugin when its matching release is unavailable and never let an unfinished migration block recovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two reproduced update/recovery failures: an unfinished plugin migration rejects the package installation needed to repair it, and a missing core-matched ClawHub release never reaches the official package's declared npm alternative.

Refs #166554. Reported by @CodeForcer.

**The reported deletion is NOT yet reproduced.** The reporter's legacy `~/.openclaw/extensions/codex` layout is a leading hypothesis, not an established cause. We have requested the original install path and update step list. This PR is scoped to recovery admission and registry lag.

## User Impact

Plugin install/update can save a verified repair package while Doctor-owned data work remains pending; runtime activation stays deferred until that work is ready. Exact `config unset plugins.entries.<id>` succeeds with the normal config backup and leaves the data obligation pending. Doctor and update repair continue through their existing recovery entry points.

For an implicit exact-version official ClawHub target, the updater tries the catalog-declared trusted npm package at that same version. Catalog pins, newer recorded release pins, and security/integrity refusals remain authoritative. If no allowed source serves it, a verified compatible installed version stays selected with a version-skew warning and a retry instruction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The migration owner required state completion before publishing the package needed to complete it. It now separates repair publication from runtime activation and preserves unresolved and unrelated migration obligations. Config retention applies the same exact-entry-removal decision during validation and persistence.

The update owner now uses the existing source-fallback installer and payload verification, and the existing npm unavailable-release warning path also handles ClawHub records. No config, CLI, environment, dependency, or SQLite schema changes are introduced.

Removed the speculative backup scanner/restorer, Doctor/startup restoration and metadata refresh hooks, and their backup tests. The remaining prior-generation cleanup deferral belongs to repair publication: an unactivated replacement has not drained the old runtime. No new deletion-prevention guard remains.

## Evidence

The regressions were run against the pre-fix production files and failed for the expected reasons:

- Install and update refused the pending-state fixture with `Plugin settings are not ready for activation`; the config CLI rejected exact plugin-entry unset.
- With real loopback ClawHub/npm registries, missing releases produced an error instead of the keep-installed warning. When npm served 9.8, the record incorrectly stayed on ClawHub 9.7 instead of selecting npm 9.8.

The retained tests also cover newer recorded release pins, stale catalog pins, untrusted registries, integrity/security refusals, pending data work, other plugins' obligations, normal config backups, and runtime activation deferral. Existing Doctor coverage verifies that a stateless replacement cannot settle a learned state obligation.

- Touched suites: **88 tests passed in each of three single-worker runs** using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <five touched files> --maxWorkers=1`: **170.87s, 198.74s, 186.18s** wall time.
- Importer sweep: **326 selected files**, passed through the repository wrapper in their discovered order across **22 shards**, **4,265.29s** wall time. **324 files had passing tests**, and the Windows-only config-sharing file was platform-skipped on macOS. The default wrapper excludes the live-profile file, so it was invoked explicitly: **181 tests passed, two provider-live cases skipped by their existing opt-in gate**, in **33.62s**. No new skips or timeout/retry changes were added.
- Full `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged --base <merge-base>` passed in **623.91s**, including core/test type graphs, formatting, lint, dead-export and architecture guards. A focused invocation after correcting the pin fixture passed in **244.40s**. Both ran locally with the existing remote-child routing flag because campaign remote proof is off. `git diff --check` passed.

Single-worker test time from the third pass, excluding shared compiler preparation:

| Suite | Test time |
| --- | ---: |
| Config CLI integration | 32.82s |
| Plugin install/update migration integration | 50.09s |
| Post-core warning/degradation | 9.69s |
| Real npm/ClawHub publication authority | 39.13s |
| Source/lifecycle authority | 3.44s |

These suites exercise real package publication, config/SQLite writes, and rollback ownership. No individual test in the three final touched-suite runs exceeded 30 seconds. Initial shared runtime preparation was about five minutes, separate from test execution. One added pin control initially used an equal-to-core version, which existing policy deliberately normalizes to the catalog default; the corrected newer-release fixture preserves the no-npm assertion and additionally verifies the exact ClawHub request. No production pin policy changed.


Pre-existing importer costs were recorded without changing the narrow fix: database rollback (123.13s/file), update leases (158.88s/file), agent-command persistence (156.13s/file), and Doctor deferral (124.61s/file). They retain real subprocess/SQLite/publication or migration matrices. Individual existing cases took 36.26s for six native-auth turns plus restart, 45.52s for owned-service post-core handoff with native admission/IPC and reinspection (precise cost split unprofiled), and 79.18s for six Doctor auth/SecretRef CLI invocations. All passed.

The isolated P1 Codex review returned HTTP 401 without an assessment. Maintainer review of this head remains necessary under the campaign ruling. No modules were added or deleted. CI seconds are not yet available at the authoring handoff.

Diff: **18 files, +505/-77**. Production **+178/-53** (285 fewer added production lines than the previous head); tests **+313/-24**; docs **+14/-0**. Updated with a plain push; history was not rewritten.
